title: Rhubarb and orange compote with yoghurt and hazelnuts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Rhubarb, oranges, honey, natural yoghurt, hazelnuts and ground spices are all plain home-kitchen foods.

supermarket.reason: Forced rhubarb, oranges, hazelnuts and natural yoghurt are all stocked by mainstream supermarkets in January at everyday prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, grater and knife, and the techniques are toasting, simmering and peeling.

works.reason: 400g rhubarb simmered briefly with orange juice and honey, three oranges and 500g yoghurt make a sensible breakfast for four with no gaps a cook couldn't fill.

honest_times.reason: Twelve minutes covers zesting, juicing, cutting the rhubarb, peeling two oranges and chopping the nuts, and ten minutes fits toasting plus a 5 to 8 minute simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and both spices are used, and 'forced rhubarb' is the same food as the rhubarb id.

seasonal_feel.reason: January oranges and forced rhubarb are in their prime, and the oranges are a main component (zest, juice and two sliced oranges) rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit, yoghurt and nuts make a balanced breakfast, with only modest added honey.
